written: 2026-10-25, before any pipeline code, from the PDF text (pdftotext) and table layouts
notes: Each question names one or more acceptable `locations`. A retrieved chunk is RELEVANT when it matches a location: same `chapter` (ES = Executive Summary, SA = Statistical Appendix, FM = front matter), same `region` / `box` when given, and its PDF page range overlaps `pdf_pages`. `require` = 'any' (one location is enough) or 'all' (cross-section questions need every location in the top-k). `numbers` are the figures a correct answer must contain. `must_not` lists the confusable places whose facts must not appear. Printed page = PDF page − 22 for chapter pages; front matter uses roman numerals. The author (Harsh) should review every expected answer against the PDF before the first full eval.

categories.reasoning: explanation or condition within one section, or routing a country/acronym to its region
categories.cross_section: needs two or more sections (possibly different chapters or regions)
categories.arithmetic: needs a computation over stated figures; must come from the computed source
categories.refusal: not in this report; must refuse

questions.question: What is the growth outlook for South Asia in this report?
questions.expected_answer: Growth in South Asia (SAR) is expected to soften to 6.3 percent in 2026 (from 7.0 percent in 2025), mainly because of the Middle East conflict (higher energy prices, reduced oil and gas supplies, disrupted remittances and tourism). The forecast was marginally upgraded (+0.1 pp) since January, and growth is set to pick up to an average of 7 percent a year in 2027–28.
must_not: Ch. 2 cross-region overview figures for other regions

questions.question: What does Chapter 3 say about sovereign debt in developing economies?
questions.expected_answer: Chapter 3 finds that rising government debt in EMDEs leads to higher interest rates, higher debt-service payments and a greater likelihood of debt distress. Debt levels are positively and non-linearly associated with dollar-denominated sovereign spreads and domestic-currency bond yields; the rise in EMDE debt-to-GDP since 2010 is associated with increases of about 110 basis points in spreads and 30 basis points in yields. Rising advanced-economy debt adds to the pressure, and effects are larger in countries with a history of default, low credit ratings, frontier-market status, reliance on short-term debt and weak governance. EMDE government debt rose from under 40 percent of GDP in 2010 to over 70 percent. It recommends stronger revenue mobilization, more efficient spending, better debt management, domestic debt market development and, where appropriate, debt-for-development swaps.
must_not: Ch. 4 public debt in commodity exporters

questions.question: According to the executive summary, what are the main risks to the global outlook?
questions.expected_answer: Risks are skewed to the downside: a renewed escalation of hostilities or more prolonged disruptions to commodity flows could raise commodity prices further, intensify inflation and food insecurity, trigger financial stress and lower growth; if energy disruptions are more severe and come with substantial financial stress, global growth could fall to just 1.3 percent in 2026. Persistent trade policy uncertainty, geopolitical strains and weather-related shocks are also material risks. On the upside, broader AI investment and adoption could lift activity.
must_not: Ch. 1 Risks to the outlook (longer list)

questions.question: What is global growth projected to be in 2026?
questions.expected_answer: Global growth is projected to slow to 2.5 percent in 2026, from 2.9 percent in 2025, the lowest rate since the COVID-19 pandemic.

questions.question: How fast are emerging market and developing economies expected to grow this year?
questions.expected_answer: EMDE growth is expected to slow to 3.6 percent in 2026 (from 4.4 percent in 2025).

questions.question: What Brent oil price does the baseline assume for 2026?
questions.expected_answer: Brent crude is assumed to average $94 per barrel in 2026, 36 percent above 2025 and more than 50 percent above the January projection.

questions.question: What is India's projected growth for fiscal year 2026/27?
questions.expected_answer: India's growth is projected to moderate to 6.6 percent in FY2026/27 (April 2026 to March 2027).

questions.question: What is the growth forecast for East Asia and Pacific in 2026?
questions.expected_answer: Growth in EAP is projected to moderate to 4.2 percent in 2026 from 5 percent in 2025, and to edge up to 4.3 percent in 2027–28.

questions.question: What is the outlook for Europe and Central Asia?
questions.expected_answer: ECA growth is projected to decelerate to 2.1 percent in 2026, weakening in about 70 percent of economies, before picking up to 2.4 percent by 2027–28. Excluding Russia and Türkiye, growth moderates to 2.8 percent in 2026 before firming to 3.1 percent.

questions.question: What growth does the report project for Latin America and the Caribbean?
questions.expected_answer: LAC growth is projected to slow to 2.2 percent in 2026, then strengthen gradually to an average of 2.5 percent over 2027–28.

questions.question: What is the growth forecast for the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan, and Pakistan region in 2026?
questions.expected_answer: Excluding Iran, MNA growth is expected to weaken to 1.6 percent in 2026 from 4 percent in 2025, a 2.7-percentage-point downgrade from January, before recovering to an average of 4.5 percent in 2027–28.
questions.notes: Ch. 2's overview (p. 50) says 'from 3.9 percent in 2025'; the MNA section and Table 2.7 say 4 / 4.0. Either is acceptable for 2025.

questions.question: What is the outlook for SSA?
questions.expected_answer: Growth in Sub-Saharan Africa is forecast to edge down to 4 percent in 2026 (revised down 0.3 pp since January) and recover to 4.4 percent on average in 2027–28.

questions.question: How fast are low-income countries expected to grow in 2026?
questions.expected_answer: Box 2.1: LIC growth is expected to reach 5.4 percent in 2026, 0.3 percentage point lower than previously forecast, edging up to an average of 5.5 percent a year in 2027–28.

questions.question: According to Box 1.1, how has global potential growth changed over recent decades?
questions.expected_answer: Global potential growth declined from 3.6 percent a year in the 2000s to 2.8 percent in the 2010s and is projected to fall to about 2.2 percent this decade (in EMDEs, from 5.9 percent in 2000–09 to 4.1 percent in 2020–29).

questions.question: In commodity-exporting EMDEs, how do revenues and primary spending respond to a 1 percent increase in commodity prices?
questions.expected_answer: Both revenues and primary spending rise by about 0.4 percent after five years, suggesting windfalls are gradually spent rather than saved.

questions.question: What share of low- and middle-income countries are in or at high risk of debt distress?
questions.expected_answer: The share rose from 26 percent in 2015 to about 50 percent in 2026.

questions.question: What was Mongolia's year-on-year growth in the fourth quarter of 2025?
questions.expected_answer: 9.2 percent (Statistical Appendix, quarterly estimates, 25Q4).

questions.question: How much is world trade volume expected to grow in 2026?
questions.expected_answer: World trade volume (goods and nonfactor services) is projected to grow 2.9 percent in 2026, 0.7 pp higher than projected in January.
questions.notes: Location widened 2026-10-25: Ch. 1 › Global context › Global trade (p. 14) states the same 2.9 percent figure.

questions.question: How much have EMDE government debt and debt-service costs risen since 2010?
questions.expected_answer: Aggregate EMDE government debt rose from less than 40 percent of GDP in 2010 to over 70 percent, and debt-service costs from 6 percent of government revenues in 2010 to an estimated 11 percent in 2025.

questions.question: What is Brazil's growth forecast for 2026?
questions.expected_answer: Brazil's growth is projected to slow to 1.9 percent in 2026, before strengthening to 2.1 percent on average in 2027–28.

questions.question: By how much are commodity prices expected to change in 2026?
questions.expected_answer: Commodity prices are expected to rise by 22 percent in 2026, in contrast to the 7 percent decline expected in January.

questions.question: Why was South Asia's 2026 growth forecast upgraded since January despite the conflict?
questions.expected_answer: Because domestic demand was more robust and export growth stronger in several economies than expected, helped by improved access to major trading partners and lower U.S. tariffs.

questions.question: Why is China relatively insulated from the conflict's energy shock?
questions.expected_answer: Its substantial oil (petroleum) reserves, high share of renewable energy and low inflation cushion the impact, and the government has capped fuel prices.

questions.question: Why is Oman's growth expected to slow only moderately compared with other Gulf hydrocarbon exporters?
questions.expected_answer: Oman is less exposed to the conflict, primarily because its major ports are located outside the Strait of Hormuz.

questions.question: What does Box 3.1 find about hidden debt?
questions.expected_answer: Revelations of hidden government debt are associated with large and significant increases in sovereign spreads, and the episodes underscore the need to fill gaps in EMDE debt transparency.

questions.question: What does the baseline assume about shipping through the Strait of Hormuz?
questions.expected_answer: Shipping remains severely disrupted through July, resumes haltingly thereafter, and approaches pre-conflict levels by the end of the year.

questions.question: How do energy and metal exporters differ from agricultural exporters over commodity price cycles?
questions.expected_answer: In energy and metal exporters, primary balances strengthen in booms and worsen in slumps mainly through revenue swings while spending stays contained, so debt ratios fall in booms and rise in slumps. Agricultural exporters raise spending in booms, offsetting revenue gains and accumulating more lasting debt.

questions.question: Why is growth in the Russian Federation expected to slow even though it is an energy exporter?
questions.expected_answer: Higher oil revenues are expected to be directed mainly toward fiscal consolidation (reducing the fiscal deficit) amid fiscal and financial pressures, so the conflict's impact on activity is contained.

questions.question: What measures does Chapter 3 recommend to contain borrowing costs?
questions.expected_answer: Strengthening fiscal positions through stronger domestic revenue mobilization, more efficient public spending, improved debt management, support for domestic debt market development and, where appropriate, debt-for-development swaps; highly indebted governments should prioritize fiscal sustainability.

questions.question: How effective have fiscal rules been for agricultural commodity exporters, according to Chapter 4?
questions.expected_answer: They show little association with fiscal stabilization and coincide with a sharper slowdown in spending in slumps: spending growth rises about 6.2 percent in boom years but slows to 3.9 percent in slumps, reinforcing rather than dampening fiscal pressures.

questions.question: Which EMDE region is expected to grow fastest in 2026?
questions.expected_answer: South Asia (SAR) is expected to remain the strongest-performing EMDE region in 2026 and over the forecast horizon, anchored by India's robust growth.

questions.question: What growth is projected in 2026 for the region that includes Pakistan?
questions.expected_answer: Pakistan belongs to the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan, and Pakistan (MNA) region, whose growth is expected to weaken to 1.6 percent in 2026.

questions.question: What is Pakistan's growth forecast?
questions.expected_answer: Pakistan's growth (fiscal year July–June, factor cost) is estimated at 3.0 percent in FY2025/26 and forecast at 3.2 percent in FY2026/27 and 3.7 percent in FY2027/28 (Table 2.8, MNA).

questions.question: Which Sub-Saharan African economies benefit from higher energy prices?
questions.expected_answer: Oil exporters, particularly Angola and Nigeria; non-oil exporters face higher fuel, fertilizer and transport costs.

questions.question: Does the report give a growth forecast for the Islamic Republic of Iran?
questions.expected_answer: No. Forecasts for Iran beyond FY2025/26 are excluded because of an exceptionally high degree of uncertainty, and the MNA aggregate excludes Iran.
questions.notes: Not a refusal: the report states why there is no forecast.

questions.question: What are the main downside risks discussed in Chapter 1?
questions.expected_answer: Prolonged or escalating geopolitical stress (resumption of hostilities, energy infrastructure damage, impaired shipping); tighter global financial conditions (higher yields, fiscal vulnerabilities, equity repricing including AI-focused firms); resurgent trade tensions and trade policy uncertainty; and weather-related natural disasters.
must_not: Executive Summary paragraph as the only source

questions.question: Compare the 2026 growth forecasts for East Asia and Pacific and Sub-Saharan Africa.
questions.expected_answer: EAP: 4.2 percent in 2026 (down from 5.0 percent). SSA: 4.0 percent in 2026 (down from 4.1 percent). EAP is 0.2 pp higher.

questions.question: Which region is worst affected in 2026, and how does its growth compare with South Asia's?
questions.expected_answer: MNA is the worst-affected region, with growth of 1.6 percent in 2026, versus 6.3 percent in South Asia (a 4.7 pp gap).
questions.alt_locations_note: Ch. 2 overview p. 50 and Table 1.1 also carry both figures.

questions.question: Compare Pakistan's and India's projected growth for fiscal year 2026/27.
questions.expected_answer: India: 6.6 percent in FY2026/27 (April–March; SAR, Table 2.10). Pakistan: 3.2 percent in FY2026/27 (July–June; MNA, Table 2.8).

questions.question: How does growth in low-income countries compare with Sub-Saharan Africa as a whole in 2026?
questions.expected_answer: LICs (Box 2.1): 5.4 percent in 2026. SSA: 4.0 percent in 2026. LIC growth is 1.4 pp higher.

questions.question: What do the two analytical chapters say about fiscal rules?
questions.expected_answer: Chapter 3: the share of EMDEs with fiscal rules has risen but remains below advanced economies; rules tend to improve fiscal balances after adoption, especially with strong institutions. Chapter 4: credible fiscal rules are part of an integrated approach (with SWFs, fiscal councils, debt management), but rules and SWFs offer limited protection against acute spending pressures after commodity shocks.

questions.question: Do the executive summary and Chapter 3 agree on how much rising debt since 2010 has raised EMDE spreads and yields?
questions.expected_answer: Yes. Both say about 110 basis points for sovereign spreads and about 30 basis points for domestic-currency yields.

questions.question: How do Chapter 1 and Chapter 4 describe the size of the 2026 commodity price shock?
questions.expected_answer: Chapter 1: commodity prices are expected to rise 22 percent in 2026 (Brent $94/bbl, +36 percent). Chapter 4: in March–April 2026 energy prices averaged about 45 percent above their 2025 average and fertilizer prices were more than 30 percent higher.

questions.question: How are higher energy prices expected to affect inflation in South Asia versus East Asia and Pacific?
questions.expected_answer: Higher fuel, food and fertilizer costs are expected to add significantly to headline inflation in MNA and SAR in the near term, whereas inflation in EAP is expected to stay relatively contained, partly because of low initial inflation, particularly in China.

questions.question: By how many percentage points is South Asia's growth expected to slow from 2025 to 2026?

questions.question: Using the forecast table, what is MNA's average projected growth for 2027 and 2028?
